title: Engineering a Ag deposited ZnO–CaTiO 3  heterostructure for solar-driven crystal violet degradation and real wastewater remediation
content: The development of efficient solar-driven photocatalysts for treating dye-contaminated wastewater remains a challenge because of the persistence of synthetic dyes and limited solar-light utilization by conventional photocatalysts. In this study, a ternary Ag@ZnO–CaTiO3 heterostructured photocatalyst was synthesized by sequentially loading ZnO onto CaTiO3, followed by the photodeposition of Ag. The sample's optical and surface structural characteristics were accessed using XRD, SEM, HRTEM, DRS, PL, IR and Raman instrumental techniques. These results showed successful formation of the Ag@ZnO–CaTiO3 composite with enhanced properties compared to the bare catalyst. When exposed to direct sunlight, the optimized Ag@ZnO–CaTiO3 photocatalyst successfully removed 99.6% (k = 0.07113 min−1) of crystal violet (CV) from a 5 ppm solution in just 75 minutes by using only 1 mg of the catalyst, resulting in a 46.8% reduction in total organic carbon (TOC). When tested with actual textile wastewater, the photocatalyst achieved a pollutant removal rate of 96.33%. The photocatalytic degradation followed apparent pseudo-first-order kinetics, with rate constants increasing from 0.17249 h−1 for pure CaTiO3 to 0.31675 h−1 for ZnO–CaTiO3 and 0.58073 h−1 for Ag@ZnO–CaTiO3. As a result, the ternary photocatalyst demonstrated reaction rates that were roughly 3.4 and 1.8 times higher than pristine CaTiO3 and ZnO–CaTiO3, respectively. The ZnO–CaTiO3 heterostructure and photodeposited Ag enhances solar light usage, interfacial charge separation, and plasmon-assisted charge-transfer processes. These results highlight the potential of Ag@ZnO–CaTiO3 as an effective solar-responsive photocatalyst for partial mineralization and degradation of industrial effluent containing dyes.
